title: Instrument cache
context: Caches instrument details and live prices in Redis with Spring Cache, to take load off the database and the price service. The quote screen calls view() for every instrument a user opens; users can pick their display currency.

refs.title: Why self-invocation skips Spring proxies: @Transactional in depth (Marco Behler)

points.title: @Cacheable bypassed by self-invocation
points.why: view() calls the cached methods on the same object, which skips Spring's proxy. Nothing is ever cached, so every request still hits the database and the price service.
points.fix: Move the cached methods into a separate bean and call them through it.

points.title: Cache key ignores the currency
points.why: The price is cached by ticker only, so a user who wants EUR can get the USD price someone else requested first.
points.fix: Include every argument in the key (drop the custom key, or use key = "#ticker + ':' + #currency").

points.title: Live prices cached with no expiry
points.why: Spring's Redis cache has no TTL by default, so a price stays cached forever and users trade on stale quotes.
points.fix: Configure a per-cache TTL (a second or two for prices, longer for instrument details) with RedisCacheConfiguration.entryTtl, or don't cache live prices.

points.title: KEYS blocks Redis
points.why: KEYS scans the whole keyspace in one go. Redis is single-threaded, so in production it stalls every other client until it finishes.
points.fix: Use the cache's own clear() (configured to use SCAN), or SCAN with a cursor, or version the key prefix.

points.title: Cache stampede on hot keys
points.why: When a popular price expires, every concurrent request misses at once and they all call the price service.
points.fix: Use @Cacheable(sync = true) so one caller loads the value per instance, or refresh hot keys ahead of expiry.
